source.title: Robust MLLM Unlearning via Visual Knowledge Distillation
source.authors: Yu-Hang Wang; Zhen-Xing Niu; Haoxuan Ji; Guangyu He; Hai-Chang Gao; Gang Hua

record.file_problem: The main paper text is present, but the appendices it refers to (including further relearning results in Appendix C) are absent.
record.tranche_reason: Tests relearning-attack robustness in the new setting of multimodal visual-knowledge unlearning.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a five-epoch relearning attack using subsets of forgotten visual data. Table 4 reports Forget VQA scores for the 20% setting described in the text. Other reported unlearning benchmarks are not extracted here because the flattened multi-benchmark table does not reliably support assigning all values to model, benchmark, and metric.
record.test_reason: The study runs a relearning attack that fine-tunes on forgotten visual data for three multimodal unlearning methods (MMU, MANU, and its own VKD), and reports Forget VQA recovery over 5 epochs (Table 4). This bears on B in a new multimodal setting, and on F for the proposed method.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that VKD resists relearning: with 20% of forgotten visual data, Forget VQA rises only from 29.3 to 30.6 (AG 1.3), while MMU and MANU recover more (AG 8.3 and 4.3). They also say more knowledge returns as the relearning fraction grows.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes multimodal visual-knowledge unlearning using visual knowledge distillation, selective neuron pruning, FIM-based masking, and fine-tuning of the visual module; the relearning attack fine-tunes on forgotten visual data.
record.method_sensitivity: Relearning results vary by method and epoch; the paper also reports attacks using 10%, 20%, and 30% of forgotten visual data, but the displayed Table 4 results correspond to the 20% setting.
record.problems: Table 4 provides no uncertainty estimates and does not state the model checkpoint or exact number of relearning examples. The chance-level reference is not given. Additional robustness results are referred to in the missing Appendix C.
record.rows_left_out: Unlearning benchmark and utility results in Table 1 are not extracted because the flattened multi-benchmark layout does not reliably support matching all values to model, benchmark, and metric. Forget QA attack results are outside the visual-knowledge recovery versions recorded here.

untested.parts: Table 1 reports forget/utility results (e.g., Forget VQA 45.8 to 29.8 for LLaVA on MLLMU-Bench), but these are not extracted as rows (declared). No chance level is stated.

Only relearning on a subset of the forgotten visual data was tested. Unrelated or loosely related relearning data, and text-only facts, were not tested. The 10% and 30% results sit in the missing Appendix C.
No direction ablation or access-versus-deletion analysis.
No prompting, jailbreak, language or in-context attacks.
Robustness was shown only against one relearning attack, in one apparent model/benchmark setting. No other attacks were tried.

missing.what: Vanilla (pre-unlearning) Forget VQA reference (45.8 for LLaVA-1.5-7B on MLLMU-Bench), needed to judge how much of the forgotten gap relearning restores. The model and benchmark behind Table 4 are also unstated.
Relearning results with 10% and 30% of forgotten data; the text says more knowledge is recovered as the fraction grows.

record.verdict_notes: The A link is removed from the Ours rows; A's evidence is Table 1, which was declared left out. Row states are judged for B (recovery), and absent or near-absent recovery for Ours is what F predicts. Table 4's 'Original' column is the unlearned, pre-attack score, not the vanilla model's, despite the AG definition's wording. The Forget QA rows in Table 4 measure retained textual knowledge, not recovery of forgotten knowledge, so leaving them out is reasonable. Table 4 reports no uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: The paper evaluates visual unlearning, utility, and relearning resistance, but does not state a chance-level reference. Benchmark values for unlearning and utility are not extracted here.
Tests relearning from forgotten visual data in an MLLM; does not test unrelated or loosely related examples, text-only forgotten facts, or other types of forgotten knowledge.
No activation-direction ablation or experiment testing whether the method blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language, or in-context-information attack.
Robustness is tested only against relearning with forgotten visual data, not the other listed attacks.

source_check.notes: Table 4 states no model, benchmark or data fraction. The 20% comes from Section 4.5, and its Original scores (29.1/38.6/29.3) differ from Table 1 LLaVA MLLMU-Bench (31.2/41.6/29.8), so the comparison with the vanilla 45.8 is assumed. Appendix C (the 10% and 30% results) is not in the text, and Table 4 gives no uncertainty. The l1 challenges label rests on the authors' explicit statement, while r14-r15 are partial (a 1.3-point rise).

statements.correction: VKD Forget VQA 29.3 before, 27.6-30.6 over epochs 1-5 (29.2, 27.6, 27.6, 30.6, 30.6) on 20% of forgotten visual data; AG 1.3.
MMU 29.1 to 37.4 (AG 8.3) and MANU 38.6 to 42.9 (AG 4.3) after 5 epochs on 20% of forgotten visual data.
statements.problem: MMU/MANU only named in conditions; rows r1, r3 are correct partial recoveries (MMU 29.1 to 31.2 at epoch 1, 37.4 at epoch 3).

statements.correction: This study: VKD on 7B MLLMs (LLaVA-1.5-7B, Qwen2-VL-7B; model and benchmark for Table 4 not stated). Relearning on 20% of forgotten visual data for 5 epochs: Forget VQA 29.3 to 29.2 (epoch 1), 30.6 at convergence (AG 1.3), vs AG 8.3 for MMU and 4.3 for MANU. Either describe it with its own conditions or drop the citation.
statements.problem: Cites this study (r11) but gives none of its facts. Its conditions (1B-3B Llama/Qwen; TOFU, LKF, FaithUn, WMDP-cyber; mostly one epoch) do not cover this study. Only the attack type (fine-tuning on part of the forget set) fits.

statements.correction: This study's only robustness test is fine-tuning the unlearned MLLM on 20% of forgotten visual data for 5 epochs: VKD Forget VQA 29.3 to 30.6 (AG 1.3). It does not belong in a prompt-attack entry. Remove the citation or move it to a fine-tuning-attack entry.
statements.problem: Cites this study (r11) under 'prompt-level attacks only', but the study ran no prompt-level attacks. r11 is a fine-tuning relearning result, and the statement says nothing about VKD.
